Replay

Recorded authority observations

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Recovery and compatibility

Use Model.authority when gameplay must react to a change in the authorized runner's local player seat, such as transferring an item carried by a departed host. The runner records its local seat as simulation input, and the game's policy applies that observation during a step:

Odin
authority = {id = 1, apply = observe_authority}

The server records Authority_Observation{known=true, seat=local_seat} in each Batch. Seat zero identifies a dedicated authority with no local player. The policy runs after fresh-player resets and before the ordinary model step, under the same commit gate and rollback transaction. It may change state and emit game events, or abort the entire tick. The policy's nonzero identifier participates in the negotiated model/checkpoint contract; change it when its semantics change.

Store the previous observed authority in game state when the rule depends on a transition. The callback can then compare recorded observations without querying the process's live role. Repeated observations leave the result unchanged, and correction restores the prior identity with the rest of the world. Cavecrawl uses this to adopt a departed host's carried relic while preserving avatars' returning player identities.

Clients record an unknown observation and do not predict authority-policy calls. They receive the resulting world through authority snapshots and gameplay occurrences through facts. Gameplay packets expose no client-supplied authority observation. An unknown observation must have seat zero; known observations require an enabled policy and an in-range seat. Recording preflight checks these rules before any simulation. Other simulation inputs continue predicting normally.

Recovery and compatibility#

server_restore retains the exact checkpoint frame. On the first subsequent committed tick, the server records its newly authorized local seat. No hidden checkpoint edit or unrecorded gameplay callback runs during restore. A checkpoint captured before that first tick still contains the old game-state observation and the current host seat in its existing header; another restore therefore does not lose a pending identity transition. The game decides how a dedicated successor or an initially unknown authority affects its entities.

Existing gameplay packet and checkpoint envelope formats are unchanged. Models with the policy disabled retain their previous negotiated contract. An enabled policy has a distinct contract, and games adding observation fields to their worlds must explicitly convert their old state schemas.

Batch is also the diagnostic recording input type, so its schema fingerprint has changed for all network recordings. Normal recording decode rejects the old fingerprint. recording_upgrade_without_authority explicitly maps older inputs only for models whose authority policy remains disabled; it cannot fabricate missing host observations. It preserves the source context, frames, decisions and events. Verification remains separate from conversion. See recording conversion.

This observation identifies the runner's local player seat. It does not represent all shared-authority object ownership, grant permission to host, or replace the lease/coordinator checks that authorize a runner to commit.
